## Citation

Budd, R.C., Scharer, C.D., Barrantes-Reynolds, R., Legunn, S., & Fortner, K.A. (2022). T Cell Homeostatic Proliferation Promotes a Redox State That Drives Metabolic and Epigenetic Upregulation of Inflammatory Pathways in Lupus. *Antioxidants & Redox Signaling*, 36(7-9), 410-422.

## Abstract

Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is characterized by aberrant T cell function and uncontrolled inflammation. This study elucidates how homeostatic T cell proliferation drives metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic changes that promote inflammatory responses in lupus pathogenesis.

## Key Findings

- Homeostatic proliferation induces a pro-oxidant redox state in T cells
- Metabolic reprogramming enhances glycolytic and oxidative pathways
- Epigenetic modifications (histone acetylation, DNA methylation) promote inflammatory gene expression
- These mechanisms drive lupus-like disease manifestations in experimental models

## Role

As a co-author, I contributed statistical and bioinformatics analysis of omics data, including epigenetic and metabolic profiling.
